apps.localizedDescription:
Paladala 係一個用 SwiftUI 寫嘅第三方嗶哩嗶哩 iOS 客戶端,目標係「淨」同「快」：

- 內置 FFmpeg 解冩 DASH 直播流,實時彈幕接力
- AVPlayer 全硬件加速播普通視頻,零額外依賴
- 完整支援 B 站帳號登入、追番、動態、收藏夾、私訊
- 影片可下載到本機離線睇
- 對 LiveContainer 友善,塞入 LiveContainer 之後唔佔 iOS 嘅 3 app 側載限額

versions.localizedDescription:
auto-bump CFBundleShortVersionString on every prerelease


The build number (CFBundleVersion) was already auto-bumped on
every CI run by reading the latest prerelease tag from the GitHub
Releases API. The marketing version (CFBundleShortVersionString)
was hard-coded — the in-app About page always read whatever was
committed (most recently '0.5.1 TESTING') regardless of how many
builds the CI had shipped. The tag-extraction regex in 'Resolve
release tag' stripped the 'TESTING' suffix, so the prerelease
tags were clean (v0.5.1.301 etc.) but the in-app display was not.

This adds a 'Bump marketing version' step right before 'Bump
build number' that applies the same auto-derive logic to the
marketing version:

  * reads the latest prerelease tag from the Releases API
  * if the tag is v<X>.<Y>.<Z>.<N> (the active line), bumps Z
    to Z+1 for the next prerelease
  * falls back to the committed Info.plist's numeric prefix
    with patch +1 when the API call fails OR the latest tag is
    in a legacy shape (v0.4.<N>, v0.5-beta-ios-<N>, …) — never
    regresses on a single bad run

The new value is written to Info.plist in the runner's working
copy only (no commit, no push) so the latest tag on the server
remains the persistent state — same pattern as the existing
build-number bump.

Trade-off: every push to working ticks the marketing patch
component up by 1 (0.5.1 → 0.5.2 → 0.5.3 …). If the user wants
to ship a real 0.6 / 1.0 release cut, they bump the major/minor
in Info.plist by hand and the auto-derive continues from there.

un-ignore release-notes/*.md so the Plan C step can commit


Build 8bb98176 failed in the 'Extract clean release notes' step
with:

  The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
  release-notes/v0.5.1.300.md

Root cause: .gitignore's blanket '*.md' rule (added for the docs
whitelisting scheme) is not specific enough — it caught the
release-notes markdown files the new CI step writes, and 'git add'
refused to stage them.

Two fixes:

* .gitignore — add a '!release-notes/' and '!release-notes/*.md'
  whitelist next to the existing docs whitelist so the files are
  intended git content. Comment explains why they're meant to be
  tracked (consumed by generate_apps_json.py at build time).

* ios-unsigned-ipa.yml — switch 'git add' to 'git add -f' as a
  safety net. If a future ignore-rule change accidentally re-blocks
  these files, the failure mode becomes an explicit 'git add -f'
  rejection rather than a silent skip-and-empty-commit; the intent
  is loud and obvious in the step log.

## Based on commit

- Commit: `60b763a0c2fea97519b5b55afdbc95c757c2a737`

### Commit description

feat(ios): in-app update check via AltSource, AltStore URL-scheme install

Replace the GitHub Releases API poll in AboutView's UpdateChecker
with a fetch of the same apps.json the AltStore / SideStore source
already serves from gh-pages. The install side now hands the
unsigned IPA URL to a sideload store via its URL scheme
(altstore://install?url=… or sidestore://install?url=…) instead
of going through a Shortcut, so users without the Shortcut
installed can update with one tap.

* Info.plist: add LSApplicationQueriesSchemes for altstore +
  sidestore so canOpenURL returns the right answer.
* UpdateManager.installLatestFromStore(downloadURL:) — new main-
  actor method that picks AltStore, falls back to SideStore, and
  finally opens the AltSource page in Safari when neither is
  installed. New InstallState / InstallPath enums.
* UpdateChecker in AboutView: parse gh-pages apps.json, match
  app by bundleIdentifier, compare full versions via
  VersionComparator. Old GitHub ReleasePayload is gone.
* UpdateState: updateAvailable / devBuild now carry downloadURL:
  URL? (the unsigned IPA URL) instead of an html_url.
* AboutView.installButton: branched on downloadURL — primary
  path is the URL-scheme install; missing-downloadURL edge case
  falls back to the legacy Shortcut flow so a tester with an
  empty source still has a way forward.
* Localizable.swift: 6 new strings (openInAltStore,
  openInSideStore, opening, noStoreDetected, viewOnGitHub,
  checkSourceHint).
* AppVersionTests: round-trip a sample AltSource manifest
  through the new decoder to guard against silent schema drift.
